# 71.64 The Warranted Conclusion Stated with Full Force

The conclusion may now be stated without postponement and without inflation.

An accepted heresy is an erroneous doctrine that a body has received as its ordinary teaching or installed in the forms by which it orders belief, worship, and discipline.

**The how** is inspectable. Erroneous doctrines become normalized when they are the way a people go, the manner of fathers and children, the path many follow, the doctrine held, the report gloried in, the arrangement loved. They become institutionalized when they are given altars, priests, a devised calendar, a unanimous official mouth, a chapel, a seat and a burden, a school’s name, an agreement and a penalty, a council’s command, a false sending, a permission to teach, a roll enforced by expulsion, or a set of prohibitions taught as the rule. Inheritance, likeness to the true worship, custody of the law’s name, and titles of prophecy or depth are the ordinary clothes of the settlement. The clothes are not the transformation.

**The why** is equally inspectable. Institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth because truth is conformity to reality and acceptance is not that conformity; because the Scripture is not broken by the bodies that teach against it; because the writings judge these doctrines inside the scenes of their greatest acceptance; because a sign that comes to pass is still denied the power to license other gods; and because patience, procedure, survival, and expulsion do not mint truth. The Graphē remains the primary written authority over the settled doctrine. The church as church is not infallible. The chapel is not the writing. The fathers are not the book.

**The contrary** is real. Do not follow a multitude to do evil. Do not hearken to the successful false prophet. Speak what the Lord says rather than what the four hundred say. Hear the book against the fathers. Obey God rather than men. Believe all that is written rather than the accuser’s name. Withstand a walk that is not upright according to the truth of the gospel. Hate the deeds Christ hates. Do not hold the doctrine he hates. Do not be shaken by a letter as from the apostles. Hold what they actually taught. The rest who have not this doctrine are not a fiction. Refusal is obedience, because the acceptance did not create a new truth to which refusal would be unfaithful.

This continues Movement IX. It is not Chapter 70 retried. It is not Chapters 72–73. It is not Movement X. That is this chapter’s conclusion, stated here with full force.

Thus:

> **How erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized has been examined, and why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth has been shown. The acceptance is in force. Later questions remain later because they are different questions.**

# 71.65 Apply the Standard

The standard has been applied.

A doctrine that has become the ordinary teaching of a body is now to be asked not only, “What truth was left, and by what mechanism?” — Chapter 70’s question — but, “Has this erroneous teaching become what the body holds, ordains, loves, commands, or will not depart from, and is that reception being offered as if it were the truth?” Was a feast devised, and is likeness to the authorized feast being treated as identity? Do the official mouths agree, and is agreement being treated as the word of the Lord? Is the place cited as the reason the contrary word must stop? Do the people love the arrangement? Do the wise say the law is with them while the word is rejected? Is the fathers’ manner the argument? Are commandments of men being taught for doctrines? Is a school’s doctrine the leaven the disciples were told to beware? Is confession punished, and is the punishment being treated as discernment? Did a requirement travel under a sending the senders deny? Are many following, and is the way of truth the thing now evil spoken of? Does a church suffer a teacher and call the suffering patience or depth? Does a prohibition of what God created present itself as the stricter faith?

The questions are practical without becoming a tribunal’s handbook, a history of later parties, or a technique of interpretation. A people who confess that Scripture is primary may still depart not from a sin a founder installed. A church addressed as a church may still hold a doctrine Christ hates. A ruler may believe and still leave the public doctrine in place for love of the institution’s praise. A research document may warn against accepted heresies and still offer its own grid for acceptance under the warning’s name. A hard sentence of Scripture may still be hard without being a human ordinance, and a human ordinance may still be severe without being Scripture.

The standard also protects. Reception of the apostles’ doctrine is not an accepted heresy. A party-name in an accuser’s mouth is not a verdict. An open question is not a calf. A servant who speaks according to the writing is not a Nicolaitan by having an office. A remnant that does not have the doctrine is not faithless to the church by refusing what Christ hates. Josiah is not a faction by tearing his clothes at the book. Micaiah is not a heretic for declining to speak like the four hundred. The protection is the same fact as the judgment: the writing is the measure of both the faithful holding and the accepted error.

The standard is the Graphē. Accepted heresy is erroneous doctrine in the form of a body’s ordinary or official teaching. Institutional acceptance is not an ontological act. The openings Chapter 70 named do not, by being inherited in a feast or a school, move the standard.

Thus:

> **The standard has been applied: how erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized, and why that acceptance does not transform error into truth, have been identified as Movement IX’s sixth word, not announced as a slogan, and not postponed as if the settlement were weak.**

# 71.66 From Accepted Heresies to Aridity

A settlement, now controlled as an inspectable reception that does not create truth, still leaves a further question.

The acceptance-file is in force. Erroneous doctrines become ordinary and official by the operations exhibited. Acceptance does not transform them. The writing remains the measure. Refusal remains possible. Those sentences are the cleared ground. They are not yet the dedicated examination of aridity in connection with deficient intellectual engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word.

If the acceptance were not stated, the next question would still be how error becomes the house’s doctrine. The acceptance has been stated. If this chapter were already the account of aridity, the next file would be repetition. This chapter is not that account. The next question is therefore the dryness the locked assignment names: Aridity and the Loss of Reasonability.

A people can love to have the false arrangement, can count the great things of the law a strange thing, can be deceived by fair speeches, and can call the strange thing wisdom because the background has trained them. Those facts raise the question of judgment. They do not answer it. The leaflet placed aridity before the heresies in its own sentence. The book’s order is the order the turning and the acceptance have now earned: after a doctrine has become the ordinary teaching, the intellectual condition in which a body can no longer tell reasonability from the chapel’s voice is a further object. Chapter 72 must examine that condition. It must not steal this settlement as if the how of acceptance had not been stated. This file must not steal the dryness as if dullness, poor judgment, and the failure to labour had already been the chapter.

That is the proper open of the next chapter. The acceptance was never meant to be a slogan that finishes Movement IX, and it was never meant to deny that settled error has an intellectual interior. It was meant to be the naming of normalization and institutionalization, and of the non-transformation, sufficient to justify taking the next question, which is the question the movement itself forces once the doctrine is ordinary and the ordinary has not become true: what is the aridity, the loss of reasonability, that stands in connection with deficient intellectual engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word?

The next file must not treat this acceptance as if the settlement had not been described. This file must not treat that aridity as if Chapter 72 were already written. Naming the neighbourhood is not performing the examination.

# What Has Been Established

This chapter has established:

1. **Accepted heresy, in this argument, is an erroneous doctrine that a body has received as its ordinary teaching or installed in the forms by which it orders belief, worship, and discipline.**
2. **Normalization is the error become the usual teaching. Institutionalization is the error set into place, office, calendar, official speech, penalty, or permission to teach. Either mode, or both, is the acceptance.**
3. ***Hairesis* ranges from party-name to fleshly faction to destructive choice. *Hairetikos* names the settled chooser. *Didachē* names the teaching held or not held. The words stay distinct. The assigned object is one.**
4. **Acceptance is not the turning retried, not governance retried, not the rank of institutions retried, not every corporate reception, and not every open question.**
5. **Reception of what the writing gives is not an accepted heresy. A hostile sect-name does not make it one.**
6. **Truth is conformity to reality. Acceptance is a fact about a body. It is not an act that conforms an error to reality.**
7. **The Scripture is not broken by a settled contrary doctrine. The Graphē remains the measure of the chapel, the council, the school, and the fathers.**
8. **The settlement is inspectable because the writings exhibit the operations. It is not a fog that follows turning.**
9. **Refusal is a real contrary. The accepted state is not fate.**
10. **Exodus 23:2 forbids following a multitude to do evil. Number does not transform.**
11. **Deuteronomy 13 denies transforming power to a sign that comes to pass, where the doctrine is other gods.**
12. **Judges 17–18 exhibits a tribal image-cult with priests, lasting until the captivity beside Shiloh. A Levite does not certify the shrine.**
13. **Jeroboam’s installation — calves, non-Levitical priests, a feast like Judah’s, a month devised of his heart — became a sin the people went to and later kings departed not from. Likeness and continuance do not transform the sin.**
14. **Second Kings 17 exhibits generational syncretism: the Lord’s name, the nations’ gods, the fathers’ manner, unto this day. The mixture is not the commandment.**
15. **The four hundred with one mouth do not make a favorable oracle true. Micaiah’s measure is what the Lord says.**
16. **The king’s chapel is cited to stop the word. The citation is the accepted cult’s self-defense, not its justification.**
17. **Judah loves a false prophetic-priestly order, claims the law while rejecting the word, and hears a standing peace-oracle. Love, pen, and repetition do not transform the vision of the prophets’ own heart.**
18. **A people can make the liar who prophesies wine into their prophet. The appointment does not make the lie the Lord’s word.**
19. **The book found in the house judges the fathers’ not-hearkening. Antiquity of practice is not the covenant.**
20. **Calling evil good does not move the evil. Fear of the Lord taught by the precept of men is still human precept.**
21. **Teaching the commandments of men for doctrines is vain worship. The elders’ acceptance does not make the tradition the commandment of God.**
22. **Breaking a commandment and teaching men so institutionalizes the breach as instruction.**
23. **The doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees is leaven to beware of. A school’s ownership of a doctrine does not make the doctrine safe.**
24. **Moses’ seat does not sanctify burdens and inversions bound from it. What is Moses is to be kept because it is Moses.**
25. **An agreement to expel confessors of Christ can be the enforceable public doctrine, even where some rulers believe. The agreement does not make non-confession true.**
26. **A council’s command not to teach in the name of Jesus does not become God’s will. God is to be obeyed rather than men. Survival in time is not the test.**
27. **A requirement can be received as a sending body’s doctrine when that body gave no such commandment. “From us” does not transform an added condition of salvation.**
28. **The way which they call heresy may be the way that believes all that is written. Institutional names do not decide, in either the hostile or the flattering direction.**
29. **Heresies among a church manifest the approved. They do not approve the faction. The “must” is not a blessing of party-making.**
30. **A respected company can be carried into a public walk contrary to the truth of the gospel. The company’s weight does not amend the gospel.**
31. **Heresies are works of the flesh. Habituation does not reclassify them as fruit.**
32. **What is commonly reported and gloried in is not thereby lawful. Corporate pride is an aggravation of acceptance, not a sanctification.**
33. **Fair speeches can make a line contrary to the doctrine learned seem acceptable to the simple. The learned apostolic doctrine remains the measure.**
34. **Ordinances of men become a body’s rule by a show of wisdom and humility. The show does not change their human origin.**
35. **Forbidding marriage and commanding abstinence from meats does not change the goodness of what God created to be received. A stricter-sounding rule is not thereby the truth.**
36. **Many follow destructive heresies, and the way of truth is evil spoken of. The following normalizes the error and slanders the truth. It does not move the name “truth.”**
37. **The heretical man, after two admonitions, is rejected as already subverted and self-condemned. Patience does not sanctify his line. Rejection does not create its falsity.**
38. **Casting out of the church can enforce a refusal of the apostle and the brethren. The purged roll is not the truth’s report.**
39. **A church can harbor holders of a doctrine Christ hates and can suffer a self-named prophetess to teach. His hate stands. Space to repent is not approval. The rest who have not this doctrine are addressed as such.**
40. **A letter as from the apostles can be the instrument of a false account. Believing a lie does not make the lie truth. The holding commanded is of what was actually taught.**
41. **The operations of settlement stack and are often inherited. Inherited piety is the interior feel of accepted heresy. It is not a second measure.**
42. **Record of a false doctrine in Scripture does not sanction it. Institutional acceptance, a weaker event, does not sanction it either.**
43. **Disharmony with what is written detects an accepted heresy in the house where it is ordinary. A verse-count and a dispensational grid are not adopted as the detector.**
44. **An accepted background can make the written law seem strange and can teach men to explain the commandment away. The strangeness does not transform the altars into the law.**
45. **The Aletheia sentence is received where accepted heresies are called doctrines, where age and a Christian name do not shield a body, and where the measure remains the Graphē. It is not adopted as a finished chain through aridity, *apeiros*, and *spoudazō*.**
46. **A warning against accepted heresies does not certify the doctrines that follow it. The grid is refused the office of replacement orthodoxy.**
47. **“The multitude transforms the error” fails.**
48. **“The fathers and the age transform the error” fails.**
49. **“Office, chapel, seat, and penalty transform the error” fails.**
50. **“A successful sign or survival in time transforms the error” fails.**
51. **“The name transforms the doctrine” fails, both when the name flatters and when the name accuses.**
52. **“Acceptance is harmless because the truth still stands” fails.**
53. **“Every sect-name is an accepted heresy” fails, and “every minority is faithful” fails.**
54. **Treating Chapters 68 and 69 as already this file fails.**
55. **Treating this chapter as already Chapter 70, or as already Chapters 72–73 or Movement X, fails.**
56. **What is explicit has been distinguished from what is inferred, and later doctrines have not been inferred here.**
57. **The acceptance attaches to an erroneous doctrine received as ordinary or official. It does not confiscate faithful holding, service under the writing, or the refusal of a settled error.**
58. **This chapter continues Movement IX because its assigned word has been stated.**
59. **This chapter opens Chapter 72 by naming the next necessary question without answering it.**
60. **What is reserved is Chapters 72–73; entire Movement X (Chapters 74–85); the First Principles themselves; and σπουδάζω (*spoudazō*) as a dedicated chapter.**

# Chapter Summary

> **The chapter’s central conclusion:** An accepted heresy is an erroneous doctrine that has become a body’s ordinary teaching or its installed rule. Because truth is conformity to reality and is not institutional consensus; because the writing is the primary written authority already earned; because that authority has been distinguished from the authority of interpretation; because the record does not fail and the Scripture cannot be broken; because misreading has been catalogued without making the writing obscure; because secondary systems have been ranked as servants; because governance of meaning has been shown as occupation of the seat of sense; and because doctrinal turning aside has been shown in its causes and mechanisms — the settlement of error can be read from the writings themselves, and the settlement can be denied the power to make error true. Installation, unison, the chapel, popular love, claimed possession of the law, the fathers’ manner, teaching human commandments as doctrines, school-doctrine, penalty, assembly-command, false sending, social carrying-away, the following of many, holding and suffering, religious show, standing prohibitions, and borrowed names carry the acceptance. Refusal of the multitude, of the successful false prophet, of the unanimous mouth, of the fathers’ neglect, of the council’s silence, and of the doctrine Christ hates remains a real contrary. Competing reductions fail: consensus; antiquity; office; survival; names; harmlessness; sect-labels and minority-romance; rank and governance as a substitute for this file; this file as a reprint of the turning or as a premature writing of aridity, unskill, and labour. The investigator is warranted, with full force, in receiving this as Movement IX’s sixth word. The acceptance is in force. Chapter 72 remains later because it is a later question. Movement IX continues.

The essential architecture is:

> **Turning already stated → accepted heresies defined → normalization and institutionalization distinguished → biblical words collected → objects distinguished → one clean account of sequence and limits → three members of positive warrant → exhibitions of settlement examined → operations joined → non-transformation gathered → reconstructible Introduction and Aletheia propositions tested → reductions refused → acceptance warranted → sequence to aridity.**

The governing distinctions are:

- **The acceptance** is not **a second account of turning.**
- **Normalization** is not **institutionalization,** and either can constitute the settlement.
- **A party-name** is not **a destructive heresy.**
- **Reception of the given word** is not **an accepted heresy.**
- **A hostile name** is not **a verdict.**
- **A flattering name** is not **a transformation.**
- **Likeness to the true feast** is not **identity with it.**
- **Custody of the law’s name** is not **hearkening to the law.**
- **The chapel’s status** is not **the word’s permission to be silent.**
- **The fathers’ manner** is not **the book’s verdict.**
- **The many’s following** is not **the way of truth.**
- **Space to repent** is not **approval.**
- **Procedure** is not **an ontological act.**
- **The truth’s survival** is not **the acceptance’s harmlessness.**
- **A minority** is not **automatically faithful.**
- **Rank and governance** are not **already this file.**
- **The strange law and the deceived simple** are not **already aridity and *apeiros*.**
- **The warner’s grid** is not **the replacement orthodoxy.**
- **This file** is not **Chapter 70 retried.**
- **This file** is not **Chapters 72–73.**
- **This file** is not **Movement X or the First Principles.**
- **Using Chapters 57, 62–63, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, and 70** is not **reprinting them.**
- **Limits** are **the shape of the doctrine**, not **delayed doubt.**
- **Sequence** is **not hesitation about this level.**

The decisive principle is:

> **Examine how erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized, and why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth, claiming what the writings’ own exhibitions and the preceding premises warrant and not more: the settlement is inspectable, the reception is not an ontological act, the truth remains the measure, and refusal is a real contrary — before examining aridity and the loss of reasonability. Draw the conclusion the premises support. Do not draw the conclusions that still require later premises. Then ask what dryness of judgment stands in connection with deficient intellectual engagement and failure to labour properly in the Word.**

## Chapter Assignment

Chapter 71 established Movement IX’s sixth word. An accepted heresy is an erroneous doctrine that a body has received as its ordinary teaching or installed in the forms by which it orders belief, worship, and discipline. The settlement is inspectable. Institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth. Truth remains conformity to reality. The Graphē remains the measure. Refusal of the multitude, the chapel, the fathers’ manner, and the suffered teacher remains a real contrary. The acceptance-file is in force.

Chapter 71 ended by naming the next necessary question, not a new curiosity:

> **What is aridity, and what is the loss of reasonability, now that erroneous doctrines have been shown becoming the ordinary and official teaching of a body without becoming true, and now that the next file’s first word is to be that dryness rather than a second acceptance-file, and rather than unskillfulness?**

That is this chapter’s assignment.

The locked Table of Contents states the work in one sentence:

> **Examine aridity in connection with deficient intellectual engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word.**

The locked knowledge-flow places this examination after the settlement and before the dedicated examination of unskillfulness. Acceptance has been stated as acceptance. Stated acceptance still leaves the intellectual condition in which a person or a people can possess the writing, the time, the organs of hearing, and even a labour that looks like study, and still not yield the sound judgment the writing requires. A doctrine become ordinary is one object. A dryness in which engagement is deficient, judgment is poor, and the labour proper to the Word is not given, is a further object. The present file is that object, at the level the premises warrant, and not beyond it.

The present file does not re-narrate how erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized. It cites Chapter 71 as established. It does not re-narrate the causes and mechanisms of departure. It cites Chapter 70 as established. It does not re-describe the occupation of the seat of sense. It cites Chapter 69 as established. It does not re-rank theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution. It cites Chapter 68 as established. It does not re-catalog how Scripture is misread. It cites Chapter 67 as established. It does not re-draw the distinction between the authority of the text and the authority of interpretation. It cites Chapter 66 as established. It does not re-prove that the Graphē is the primary written authority. It cites Chapter 65 as established. It does not re-answer why the Scripture cannot be broken, or why the record does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates. It cites Chapters 62–63 and 57 as established. It does not write *apeiros* as a dedicated file. It does not write Movement X. It does not enter the First Principles. It examines aridity in its three assigned connections, without which Movement IX would possess a settlement and still lack the earned account of the dryness in which reasonability is lost.

A settlement, now distinguished from a mere turning and from a mere disagreement, still leaves a further question. If a body can teach an error as its doctrine without making the error true, what is the condition of hearing and judgment in which that doctrine can be lived as though it were the reasonable thing, and in which the writing, though given, does not yield in the hearer the consideration, the discrimination, and the labour it commands? If the dryness were already the settlement restated, the sixth word would be reprinted as the seventh. If the dryness were already the diagnosis of the unskillful, or already the method of diligence, the later files would be closed inside this one. If the examination stopped at the warning “do not be dull,” the connections would be a slogan. The present file is the aridity, at the level the writings and the locked assignment require, and not beyond it.

The remaining question of the book’s sequence follows. Sequence continues the investigation. It does not convert the present line into hesitation.

## Central Objective

> **To examine, from the biblical record and from premises already in force, aridity in connection with deficient intellectual engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word, so that Movement IX’s seventh word is one inspectable verdict: aridity is the dryness in which the Word is given to be heard, judged, and laboured in, and the hearer does not yield the reasonability that such engagement requires; reasonability is sound judgment already defined, and its loss is the failure of that judgment toward the writing, not the disappearance of thought and not the obscurity of the Graphē; the writings exhibit the dryness as not-considering, dull hearing, a sealed book, a famine of hearing, feeding on ashes, a mind that does not pass the test, judgment omitted, an answer before hearing, a learning that never arrives, and a search that will not come; the three connections are the assignment’s own relations, read from the exhibitions, and not a single-cause system. The Word remains water, light, and measure. The Scripture is not broken by dull ears. A correct reading remains possible. Consideration, righteous judgment, and the labour the writing commands remain real contraries. The account keeps this dryness distinct from a second narrative of acceptance, from unskillfulness as a dedicated diagnosis, and from the labour-files. It refuses the reductions that blame the writing’s difficulty, that treat dryness as harmless because the truth still stands, that treat the loss as the abolition of a correct reading, that treat judicial hardening as an excuse or as the author’s injustice, that treat ever-learning as proof of engagement, that treat the chapel’s voice as reasonability once a doctrine is ordinary, and that treat this file as already Chapter 71, Chapter 73, or Movement X. It refuses both under-claim and over-claim.**

The governing movement is:

> **Acceptance already stated → question of aridity → aridity and the loss of reasonability defined → the three connections distinguished → biblical words collected → objects distinguished → premises already in force used, not retried → one clean account of sequence and limits → positive warrant from the writing’s not being dry, from the writings’ exhibition of the dryness, and from the real possibility of the contrary → each exhibition examined with biblical record → the three connections joined → non-excuse and non-breakage stated from the exhibitions → reconstructible Introduction and Aletheia propositions tested as coherence → competing reductions refused → inspectable inference → warranted conclusion → sequence to *apeiros*.**

The chapter’s conclusion is affirmative:

> **Aridity is the dryness in which what the Graphē gives to be heard, judged, and laboured in does not yield, in the hearer, the sound judgment that engagement with that writing requires. Reasonability is that sound judgment: perception, distinction, inference, and conclusion accountable to grounds, exercised toward the writing. Its loss is not the silence of the mind. Men still reason, still learn, still claim wisdom, still search, and still tithe the small exactness. The loss is the failure of those acts to do the work the writing assigns them. The people do not know and do not consider, though the ox knows his owner. They are famished and dried up with thirst because they have no knowledge, and they are wise in their own eyes. Their heart is gross, their ears dull, their eyes closed, and the condition can be judicial after refusal without becoming the writing’s fault or the hearer’s excuse. A spirit of deep sleep is poured out, and the vision is as a sealed book: the learned cannot read it because it is sealed, and the unlearned cannot because he is not learned, while wisdom perishes. The idolater feeds on ashes and does not say that a lie is in his right hand, while the same prophet says that water is poured on the thirsty and floods on the dry ground. The fountain of living waters is forsaken, and the cisterns hewed cannot hold water. The man who trusts in man inhabits the parched places and does not see when good comes. Knowledge is rejected, and the people are destroyed for the lack. A famine is sent, not of bread, but of hearing the words of the Lord, and they run to and fro and do not find it, after they have commanded the prophets not to prophesy. A matter is answered before it is heard. Wisdom cries, and the simple love simplicity, and the reproof still says, Turn. The if-clauses of seeking knowledge as silver are the form of the labour, and the labour not given is the failure. Disciples reason about bread with eyes, ears, and a memory of the baskets, and do not understand. Men are asked why they do not, even of themselves, judge what is right, and are commanded to judge righteous judgment rather than appearance, and to judge what is said. They are slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken. They search the scriptures and will not come to the one of whom the scriptures testify. Love is prayed up into knowledge and all judgment, that the excellent may be approved; the mind is to be renewed so that it may prove the will of God; and where God was not approved to be retained in knowledge, the mind given over is an unapproved mind. Judgment, mercy, and faith are omitted while mint is tithed. Some are ever learning and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth, and reprobate concerning the faith. Many things are hard to utter because the hearers have become dull of hearing, not because the things have been made mysteries. The same word that names the dullness commands, Be not slothful. The writing is not dry. Dullness does not break it. The loss does not transform an accepted error into truth, and it does not excuse the hearer who will not consider, judge, or labour. This continues Movement IX. It is not Chapter 71 retried. It is not Chapter 73. It is not Movement X. That is this chapter’s conclusion, stated here with full force.**

The remaining questions follow by sequence. The verdict is already in force as a warranted account of aridity and the loss of reasonability, not as postponed guesswork.
