# 72.55 Explicit Versus Inferred

What is explicit in the writings used here includes: the ox’s knowledge set against Israel’s not-knowing and not-considering, in a chapter that also says, Come now, and let us reason together (Isaiah 1:3, 18); captivity because the people have no knowledge, the multitude dried up with thirst, and woe on those wise in their own eyes (Isaiah 5:13, 21); hearing without understanding, a fat heart, heavy ears, shut eyes, lest they convert and be healed, cited where a people seeing see not (Isaiah 6:9–10; Matthew 13:13–15); a spirit of deep sleep, a vision as a sealed book, the learned and the unlearned both declining to read, and the wisdom of the wise perishing (Isaiah 29:9–14); water poured on the thirsty and on the dry ground, and a man who feeds on ashes and does not say that a lie is in his right hand (Isaiah 44:3, 18–20); makers of idols become like them, eyes that see not (Psalm 115:4–8); two evils, the fountain forsaken and broken cisterns that hold no water (Jeremiah 2:13); the heath in the parched places who does not see when good comes, and the tree by the waters that does not cease from fruit in drought (Jeremiah 17:5–8); destruction for lack of knowledge because knowledge was rejected and the law forgotten (Hosea 4:6); a sent famine of hearing the words of the Lord, a search that does not find, after prophets were told not to prophesy (Amos 8:11–13; Amos 2:12); wisdom crying in the streets, the simple loving simplicity, the command to turn at reproof, and the folly of answering a matter before hearing it (Proverbs 1:20–23; Proverbs 18:13); the if-clauses of receiving, crying, and searching as for silver, and the Lord giving wisdom out of his mouth (Proverbs 2:1–6); why reason ye, unused eyes and ears and memory, baskets counted, and understanding absent (Mark 8:17–21); why even of yourselves judge ye not what is right; judge righteous judgment; judge ye what I say (Luke 12:57; John 7:24; 1 Corinthians 10:15); slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken, and an exposition in all the scriptures (Luke 24:25–27); search, and ye will not come (John 5:39–40); readiness and daily search whether things are so, and a heart prepared to seek, to do, and to teach (Acts 17:11; Ezra 7:10); knowing God, vain reasonings, wisdom professed and folly become, not approving to retain God in knowledge, a giving-over to an unapproved mind (Romans 1:21–22, 28); the renewing of the mind unto proving the will of God, and love abounding in knowledge and all judgment unto approving the excellent (Romans 12:2; Philippians 1:9–10); judgment, mercy, and faith omitted while mint is tithed (Matthew 23:23); ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth, minds unapproved concerning the faith, and scriptures able to make wise unto salvation (2 Timothy 3:7–8, 15); many things hard to be uttered seeing ye are become dull of hearing, and by reason of the time ye ought to be teachers (Hebrews 5:11–12); be not slothful, but followers of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises (Hebrews 6:11–12).

What is inferred, and warranted by the join, is that these explicit relations are the aridity and the loss of reasonability the locked assignment names; that the three connections — deficient intellectual engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word — are readable across the exhibitions without being identical; that the loss is a loss after a gift, where the texts mark knowledge, time, organs, or a delivered book; that the kept forms of reasoning, learning, exactness, and hewing can be the dryness; that judicial hardening follows refusal and intensifies the condition without excusing the refusal or cancelling the command; that the writing is not the dry subject; and that consideration, righteous judgment, and seeking are real contraries.

What is not inferred here: that *apeiros* and the babe have been written; that milk, strong meat, and senses exercised to discern have been made the doctrine of maturity; that *spoudazō*, the scholarly impetus, rightly dividing, or the First Principles have been established; that Hebrews 6:1–2 has been taught; that every thirst is unbelief, or that Ezekiel’s dry bones are this condition; that every hard sentence is a dull audience; that every busy student is ever-learning in the sense of 2 Timothy 3:7; that reasoning as such is unbelief; that the seven reasons or the ten classes are a complete psychology; that a verse-count or a dispensational grid is the cure; that the leaflet’s order of causes is the book’s order; that the materials’ system is the water poured on the dry ground; that a finished theodicy of hardening has been written beyond the sequences the texts show; that every long-standing church is the Hebrews’ audience.

The distinction between explicit and inferred is itself part of the chapter’s honesty. The writings exhibit a dryness of hearing, judgment, and labour, and they judge it. The chapter names those exhibitions as the account of aridity and the loss of reasonability. The later files remain later.

Thus:

> **What the writings assign as not-considering, dull hearing, unread books, rejected knowledge, unapproved minds, and labour that does not arrive is explicit. That those relations are this chapter’s account of aridity and the loss of reasonability is the warranted inference. Later doctrines have not been inferred here.**

# 72.56 The Warranted Conclusion Stated with Full Force

The conclusion may now be stated without postponement and without inflation.

Aridity is the dryness in which the Word is given to be heard, judged, and laboured in, and the hearer does not yield the reasonability that such engagement requires.

**Reasonability** is sound judgment: the discipline that perceives, distinguishes, infers, and proves according to grounds. Its loss is not the silence of the mind. It is the failure of that discipline toward the writing. Men still reason, learn, tithe, hew, and call themselves wise. The yield is ashes, a sealed book, a counted basket and no understanding, a mint-tithe and an omitted judgment, a learning that never comes to the knowledge of the truth.

**The three connections** are inspectable. Engagement is deficient when the word, the time, the eyes, the ears, or the memory are present and the act of considering and holding is not. Judgment is poor when the discrimination does not prove what the grounds require, when it answers before hearing, when it judges by appearance, when it omits judgment, when it is wise in its own eyes, when it will not say that the lie is in the hand. Labour in the Word fails when the seeking the writings command is not given, or is given toward a cistern, a form of godliness, or a search that will not come. The three confirm one another and are not one word.

**The writing** is not dry. Hardness of utterance is located in the hearers. The Scripture is not broken by dull ears. A correct reading remains possible. An incorrect reading remains incorrect. The truth’s survival does not make the dryness harmless, and the dryness does not make an accepted error true.

**The hearer** is not excused. Not-considering, rejected knowledge, loved simplicity, the will not to come, and the ought of the time are charges. Judicial fatness, sleep, famine, and giving-over follow refusal. They are real. They are not the innocence of the first act, and they are not the injustice of the command. Be not slothful. Judge ye what is right. Turn at the reproof. Search whether those things are so.

This continues Movement IX. It is not Chapter 71 retried. It is not Chapter 73. It is not Movement X. That is this chapter’s conclusion, stated here with full force.

Thus:

> **Aridity in connection with deficient intellectual engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word has been examined, and the loss of reasonability has been shown as the failure of sound judgment toward a Word that remains clear, binding, and able to be heard. The dryness is in force. Later questions remain later because they are different questions.**

---

# 72.57 Apply the Standard

The standard has been applied.

A hearer, a priest, a school, or a people is now to be asked not only, “Has an erroneous teaching become what the body holds?” — Chapter 71’s question — but, “Is the hearing dull, the judgment unproving, the labour improper, toward a Word that is in reach?” Do they consider? Do they believe all that the prophets have spoken, or only the part that fits the hope they already had? Do they answer before they hear? Do they omit judgment while they are exact about the small clause? Do they learn without coming to the knowledge of the truth? Do they search and not come? Do they cite the seal, or the lack of learning, or the theory that the book is hard, as the reason the book stays shut? Has the time been long enough that they ought to be teachers, and are they still dull? Is the chapel’s voice the thing they can no longer tell from the writing’s reason? Is the busyness a hewing of cisterns?

The questions are practical without becoming a director’s manual, a history of mystical desolation, or a technique of study. A people who confess that Scripture is primary may still be dried up with thirst for lack of knowledge. A disciple who has seen the works may still reason and not understand. A learned man may still say, I cannot, for it is sealed. A research document may warn against dullness and still offer its grid as the water. A hard sentence may still be hard without the hearer being dull, and a dull hearer may still be dull in front of a sentence that is plain.

The standard also protects. Thirst that seeks God is not aridity. The patience that hears a matter through before answering is not poor judgment. Unfinished labour at a large book is not sloth. The tree that keeps its fruit in a year of drought is not the heath in the parched places. A beginning is not yet a loss. Service that receives the word with readiness and searches whether things are so is not the dryness it resists. The protection is the same fact as the judgment: the writing is the measure of both the hearing and the dullness.

The standard is the Graphē. Aridity is the loss of reasonability in the three connections the assignment names. The openings Chapter 71 named do not, by being intellectually untested, move the standard. The dryness does not move it either.

Thus:

> **The standard has been applied: aridity in connection with deficient engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word has been identified as Movement IX’s seventh word, not announced as a slogan, and not postponed as if the dryness were weak.**

# 72.58 From Aridity to Unskillfulness

A dryness, now controlled as an inspectable loss of sound judgment that does not make the writing obscure and does not excuse the hearer, still leaves a further question.

The aridity-file is in force. Engagement, judgment, and labour fail in the ways exhibited. The Word remains water and measure. The contrary remains possible. Those sentences are the cleared ground. They are not yet the dedicated examination of ἄπειρος (*apeiros*), unskillfulness in the Word.

If the dryness were not stated, the next question would still be what the loss of reasonability is. The dryness has been stated. If this chapter were already the account of unskillfulness, the next file would be repetition. This chapter is not that account. The next question is therefore the unskillfulness the locked assignment names, which closes Movement IX: Ἄπειρος — Unskillfulness in the Word.

Hebrews 5:13 stands in the paragraph this chapter has used and has not expounded. The dull of hearing have been examined. The one who uses milk, unskillful in the word of righteousness, for he is a babe, has not been examined. The relationship between lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word appropriately is the next file’s own sentence. The leaflet joined the two marks. The join has been named as neighbourhood. Chapter 73 must develop the second mark. It must not steal this dryness as if dull hearing had not been stated. This file must not steal the unskillfulness as if *apeiros* had already been the chapter.

That is the proper open of the next chapter. The dryness was never meant to be a slogan that finishes Movement IX, and it was never meant to deny that the dull hearer is also, in the same paragraph, described as unskillful. It was meant to be the naming of aridity and the loss of reasonability, in the three connections assigned, sufficient to justify taking the next question, which is the question the movement itself forces once hearing has been shown dull and the dullness has not been allowed to swallow the neighbouring word: what is *apeiros*, unskillfulness in the Word, and how do lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word stand together?

The next file must not treat this dryness as if the loss of reasonability had not been described. This file must not treat that unskillfulness as if Chapter 73 were already written. Naming the neighbourhood is not performing the examination.

# What Has Been Established

This chapter has established:

1. **Aridity, in this argument, is the dryness in which the Word given to be heard, judged, and laboured in does not yield, in the hearer, the reasonability that engagement requires.**
2. **Reasonability is sound judgment already defined: perception, distinction, inference, and proving accountable to grounds. The loss is the failure of that judgment toward the writing, not the disappearance of thought.**
3. **Deficient intellectual engagement is the Word, the time, the eyes, the ears, or the memory in reach, and the act of considering and holding not given, or given without coming to knowledge.**
4. **Poor judgment is discrimination that does not prove what the grounds require. It includes the answer before hearing, judgment by appearance, omitted judgment, and wisdom in one’s own eyes.**
5. **Failure to labour properly in the Word is the refusal or the evasion of the seeking, searching, meditating, and heart-preparation the writings command. A labour of the wrong object is included. The positive method of diligence is not included.**
6. **The three connections confirm one another and remain distinguishable. Aridity stands in connection with them. It is not a mood beside them.**
7. **The writing is not dry. Dullness does not break the Scripture. Hardness of utterance in Hebrews 5:11 is located in the hearers.**
8. **A correct reading remains possible. An incorrect reading remains incorrect. Despair fails again, on this chapter’s own evidence.**
9. **The dryness is inspectable because the writings exhibit it. It is not a fog that follows acceptance.**
10. **The contrary is real. Consideration, righteous judgment, turning at reproof, and seeking are commanded. The loss is not fate.**
11. **The loss does not excuse the hearer. Not-considering, rejected knowledge, loved simplicity, the will not to come, and the ought of the time are charges.**
12. **The loss does not transform an accepted error into truth. A dry mind’s sense of the reasonable is not a new ground.**
13. **Judicial fatness, deep sleep, famine of hearing, and the unapproved mind are real answers of God after refusal. They do not make the refusal innocent, and they do not make the commands unjust.**
14. **Isaiah 1:3 exhibits not-knowing and not-considering in a people still called to reason.**
15. **Isaiah 5:13 and 5:21 exhibit thirst for lack of knowledge, and wisdom in one’s own eyes.**
16. **Isaiah 6 and Matthew 13 exhibit hearing without understanding, a gross heart, and dull ears, in a judgment that costs conversion and healing, while ears that hear are still addressed.**
17. **Isaiah 29 exhibits a sealed book, two excuses that cover the field of readers, a poured-out sleep, and wisdom that perishes.**
18. **Isaiah 44 exhibits water on the dry ground and a man who feeds on ashes and cannot say that a lie is in his right hand. The truster becomes like the blind idol.**
19. **Jeremiah 2:13 exhibits a fountain forsaken and a labour of hewing cisterns that hold no water.**
20. **Jeremiah 17 exhibits the parched habitation of the man who trusts in flesh and does not see when good comes, and the tree that still yields in drought. Circumstantial drought is not this aridity.**
21. **Hosea 4:6 exhibits destruction for a lack of knowledge that was a rejection and a forgetting of the law. Fallow ground and the plowing of wickedness exhibit labour not given and labour given to the wrong end.**
22. **Amos 8 exhibits a sent famine of hearing the words of the Lord, after prophets were silenced. Running to and fro is not the labour of hearing.**
23. **Proverbs 1 and Proverbs 18:13 exhibit wisdom crying in public, simplicity loved, and the folly of answering before hearing.**
24. **Proverbs 2 exhibits the if-clauses of proper labour and the Lord as the giver. The refused if is the failure. The method-files are not written by the quotation.**
25. **Mark 8 exhibits reasoning that moves and does not yield, in disciples who can count the baskets and do not understand. Dryness is not reserved for the chapel.**
26. **Luke 12:57, John 7:24, and 1 Corinthians 10:15 assign judgment as a duty. Preference is not the canon. Refusal to judge is not humility.**
27. **Luke 24:25 exhibits slowness of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken. Partial belief is the dryness. Exposition addresses the slow heart and does not accuse the writings.**
28. **John 5:39–40 exhibits a search that will not come to the one of whom the scriptures testify. The form of labour can be the dryness.**
29. **Acts 17:11 and Ezra 7:10 exhibit the contrary labour as readiness, daily testing by the scriptures, and a heart prepared to seek, to do, and to teach. The contrary is not a curriculum.**
30. **Romans 1 exhibits an unapproved mind after a knowledge not retained and a wisdom professed. The proving-verb names both the refusal and the mind that is given over.**
31. **Romans 12:2 and Philippians 1:9–10 exhibit reasonability as the proving of the will of God and the approval of what is excellent.**
32. **Matthew 23:23 exhibits judgment omitted by men who tithe mint. Exactness is not reasonability. Proportion keeps the weightier and the lighter.**
33. **Second Timothy 3:7–8 exhibits ever learning that never comes to the knowledge of the truth, beside scriptures able to make wise unto salvation. The company’s inability is not the writing’s inability.**
34. **Hebrews 5:11 exhibits hearers who have become dull of hearing, so that many things are hard to utter. The time in which they ought to be teachers measures the loss. The subject is not a mystery.**
35. **Hebrews 6:12 forbids the same sloth and commands diligence, faith, and patience. The foundation-list is not opened. The verb of study is not spent.**
36. **Thirst that seeks God, the dry bones of Ezekiel 37, the mere hardness of a sentence, a beginning, the patience of hearing a matter through, and unfinished labour at a large book are not this aridity.**
37. **The Bible Introduction’s note on Hebrews 5:11 is received where dullness is in the hearers, the word means slowness and sloth, and time is not growth. It is not adopted as the file of *apeiros* or as the teaching of the first principles.**
38. **The seven reasons cohere as a restatement of Mark 8 and do not cohere as a condemnation of reasoning, as a complete psychology, or as a denial of judicial sleep.**
39. **Ignorance, laziness, and the theory that the book is hard cohere with unreadness. The ten classes, the witness-count, and the dispensational grid are not adopted as the cure.**
40. **The Aletheia sentence is received where reasonability is sound judgment and where that judgment’s loss stands with aridity and with failure to labour. It is not adopted as a finished chain through *apeiros*, tergiversation, accepted heresies, and *spoudazō*, and the book’s order is not rearranged to match the leaflet.**
41. **A warning against dryness does not certify the doctrines printed after it. The grid is not the water. Each sentence meets the writing.**
42. **“The writing is dry” fails.**
43. **“The dryness is harmless because the truth still stands” fails.**
44. **“The loss abolishes a correct reading” fails.**
45. **“Judicial hardening makes the commands unfair” fails, and “judicial hardening is only a figure” fails.**
46. **“Activity is engagement” fails.**
47. **“The chapel’s voice is reasonability” fails.**
48. **“Only the heart” fails, and “only the intellect” fails.**
49. **Treating this chapter as already Chapter 71, or as already Chapter 73 or Movement X, fails.**
50. **What is explicit has been distinguished from what is inferred, and later doctrines have not been inferred here.**
51. **The dryness attaches to engagement, judgment, and labour toward a given Word. It does not confiscate thirst that seeks, faithful proving, or the patience of real hearing.**
52. **This chapter continues Movement IX because its assigned word has been stated.**
53. **This chapter opens Chapter 73 by naming the next necessary question without answering it.**
54. **What is reserved is Chapter 73; entire Movement X (Chapters 74–85); the First Principles themselves; and σπουδάζω (*spoudazō*) as a dedicated chapter.**

---

# Chapter Summary

> **The chapter’s central conclusion:** Aridity is the dryness in which the Word given to be heard, judged, and laboured in does not yield the sound judgment engagement requires. Because truth is conformity to reality; because the writing is the primary written authority already earned; because that authority has been distinguished from the authority of interpretation and despair has been refused; because the record does not fail and the Scripture cannot be broken; because misreading has been catalogued without making the writing obscure; because secondary systems have been ranked as servants and governance has been shown as occupation of the seat; because turning aside has been shown in its causes; and because accepted heresies have been shown as settlements that do not create truth — the dryness can be read from the writings themselves, and it can be denied the power to obscure the Word, to excuse the hearer, or to abolish a correct reading. Not-considering, knowledge-thirst, dull organs, a sealed book, ashes, broken cisterns, parched places, rejected knowledge, a famine of hearing, the answer before hearing, unfruitful reasoning, omitted judgment, an unapproved mind, ever-learning, and dullness after time carry the loss. Consideration, righteous judgment, turning at reproof, daily search, and the command not to be slothful remain real contraries. Competing reductions fail: an obscure Bible; a harmless dryness; despair; hardening as excuse; busyness as engagement; the chapel as reasonability; the split of heart and intellect; this file as a reprint of acceptance or as a premature writing of unskill and labour. The investigator is warranted, with full force, in receiving this as Movement IX’s seventh word. The dryness is in force. Chapter 73 remains later because it is a later question. Movement IX continues.

The essential architecture is:

> **Acceptance already stated → aridity and the loss of reasonability defined → the three connections distinguished → biblical words collected → objects distinguished → one clean account of sequence and limits → three members of positive warrant → exhibitions of dryness examined → connections joined → non-excuse and non-breakage gathered → reconstructible Introduction and Aletheia propositions tested → reductions refused → dryness warranted → sequence to *apeiros*.**

The governing distinctions are:

- **The dryness** is not **a second account of acceptance.**
- **The loss of reasonability** is not **the silence of the mind.**
- **Deficient engagement** is not **an empty calendar.**
- **Poor judgment** is not **preference honestly confessed.**
- **Failure to labour** is not **the positive method of diligence.**
- **The writing** is not **the dry subject.**
- **A hard sentence** is not **a dull audience.**
- **Thirst that seeks** is not **aridity.**
- **Drought endured by the planted tree** is not **the heath in the parched places.**
- **Judicial hardening** is not **the innocence of the first refusal.**
- **The command to consider** is not **a mockery.**
- **Ever-learning** is not **coming to the knowledge of the truth.**
- **The chapel’s voice** is not **sound judgment.**
- **Dull of hearing** is not **yet *apeiros*.**
- **The time-clause** is not **the foundation-list.**
- **The noun of diligence** is not **the chapter on *spoudazō*.**
- **The warner’s grid** is not **the water.**
- **This file** is not **Chapter 71 retried.**
- **This file** is not **Chapter 73.**
- **This file** is not **Movement X or the First Principles.**
- **Using Chapters 57, 62–63, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70, and 71** is not **reprinting them.**
- **Limits** are **the shape of the doctrine**, not **delayed doubt.**
- **Sequence** is **not hesitation about this level.**

The decisive principle is:

> **Examine aridity in connection with deficient intellectual engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word, claiming what the writings’ own exhibitions and the preceding premises warrant and not more: the dryness is inspectable, the loss is a failure of sound judgment, the writing remains the measure, the hearer remains responsible, and the contrary is real — before examining *apeiros*, unskillfulness in the Word. Draw the conclusion the premises support. Do not draw the conclusions that still require later premises. Then ask what unskillfulness in the Word is, and how lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word stand together.**

---

# Transition to Chapter 73

Movement IX continues. Its seventh word has been stated.

The Graphē has been shown to be the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived. The writing is the decisive written measure. That gate is in force. The authority of that writing has been distinguished from the authority claimed for a later statement of what the writing means. Transfer fails. Despair fails. How that later act fails has been examined: poor perception, deficient understanding, faulty inference, context failure, improper handling. The writing remains the measure of those operations. Theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution have been examined as secondary systems toward that writing. They may serve under it. None becomes primary authority merely by claiming Christian identity, academic status, antiquity, or institutional recognition. What happens when commentaries, traditions, institutions, teachers, systems, or experiences govern the meaning of Scripture instead of serving under it has been examined. The seat of sense is occupied. The test is reversed. The writing is not broken. Service is not the event. The causes and mechanisms of doctrinal turning aside have been examined, and the intellectual failures that permit departure from truth have been identified. The movement is inspectable. The truth left remains the measure. Continuance is a real contrary. How erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized has been examined, and why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth has been shown. The settlement is inspectable. The reception is not an ontological act. Refusal is a real contrary. Aridity has now been examined in connection with deficient intellectual engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word. The loss of reasonability is the failure of sound judgment toward a Word that remains clear and binding. The hearer is not excused. A correct reading remains possible. Movement IX’s seventh word is in force.

The writings that judge that dryness do not leave unused the further question of skill. Dullness has been stated as dullness. Stated dullness still leaves the dedicated examination of *apeiros*, unskillfulness in the Word: the inexperienced hearer, the relation of lack of skill to immaturity, and the inability to handle the Word appropriately. A hearer can be dull of hearing, and the account of unskillfulness in the word of righteousness can remain a different question. The next necessary question is therefore not a new curiosity. It is the question the locked assignment names, and it is the question that closes Movement IX:

> **What is *apeiros*, unskillfulness in the Word, now that aridity and the loss of reasonability have been shown in connection with deficient engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word, and now that the next file’s first word is to be that unskillfulness rather than a second dryness-file, and rather than the labour-movement?**

That is the subject of:

# Chapter 73 — Ἄπειρος — Unskillfulness in the Word

> **Develop Hebrews 5:13 and *apeiros*: inexperienced/unskillful. Explain the relationship between lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word appropriately.**

The investigation now moves from:

> **aridity and the loss of reasonability**
>
> to:
>
> ***apeiros*, unskillfulness in the Word.**

Movement IX remains open until that word is stated. Movement X remains later.

# End of Chapter 72

title: Ἄπειρος — Unskillfulness in the Word
body:
> **Movement IX — When Authoritative Truth Is Mishandled**

> **Central objective:** Develop Hebrews 5:13 and ἄπειρος (*apeiros*): inexperienced, unskillful. Explain the relationship between lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word appropriately, so that Movement IX’s last word is one inspectable verdict: the one who partakes of milk is unskilled in the word of righteousness, for he is a babe, and that pair is an inability to handle the Word as the time and the word require. The Word remains handleable. After the time in which one ought to be a teacher, the condition is a charge. This closes Movement IX. It uses Chapters 57, 62–63, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70, 71, and 72 as premises. It is not a second dryness-file, and it is not Movement X or the First Principles written in advance.

---

## Chapter Assignment

Chapter 72 established Movement IX’s seventh word. Aridity is the dryness in which the Word given to be heard, judged, and laboured in does not yield, in the hearer, the sound judgment that engagement requires. Reasonability is that sound judgment. Its loss is the failure of proving, considering, and discriminating toward the writing, not the silence of the mind and not the obscurity of the Graphē. The writing is not broken by dull ears. A correct reading remains possible. The hearer is not excused. The dryness-file is in force.

Chapter 72 ended by naming the next necessary question, not a new curiosity:

> **What is *apeiros*, unskillfulness in the Word, now that aridity and the loss of reasonability have been shown in connection with deficient engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word, and now that the next file’s first word is to be that unskillfulness rather than a second dryness-file, and rather than the labour-movement?**

That is this chapter’s assignment.

The locked Table of Contents states the work in one sentence:

> **Develop Hebrews 5:13 and *apeiros*: inexperienced/unskillful. Explain the relationship between lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word appropriately.**

The locked knowledge-flow places this examination after the dryness and before the scholarly labour of the Graphē. Dullness of hearing has been stated as dullness. Stated dullness still leaves the second mark of the same paragraph: the one who uses milk, unskillful in the word of righteousness, for he is a babe. A loss of sound judgment is one object. A lack of skill in the word, standing with immaturity and with inability to handle the Word appropriately, is a further object. The present file is that object, at the level the premises warrant, and not beyond it.

The present file does not re-narrate the dryness. It cites Chapter 72 as established. It does not re-narrate how erroneous doctrines become a body’s ordinary teaching. It cites Chapter 71 as established. It does not re-narrate the causes and mechanisms of departure. It cites Chapter 70 as established. It does not re-describe the occupation of the seat of sense. It cites Chapter 69 as established. It does not re-rank theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution. It cites Chapter 68 as established. It does not re-catalog how Scripture is misread. It cites Chapter 67 as established. It does not re-draw the distinction between the authority of the text and the authority of interpretation. It cites Chapter 66 as established. It does not re-prove that the Graphē is the primary written authority. It cites Chapter 65 as established. It does not re-answer why the Scripture cannot be broken, or why the record does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates. It cites Chapters 62–63 and 57 as established. It does not write Movement X. It does not enter the First Principles. It develops Hebrews 5:13, without which Movement IX would possess a dryness and still lack the earned account of unskillfulness in the Word.

A dryness, now distinguished from a settlement and from a mere warning, still leaves a further question. If a hearer can be dull of hearing toward a Word that remains clear, what is the unskill the same paragraph names in the one who partakes of milk, and how do lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word stand together? If the unskill were already the dryness restated, the seventh word would be reprinted as the eighth. If the unskill were already the method of diligence, the stages of learning, the exercise of the senses, the doctrine of maturity, the canon-wide diagnosis of the babe, the right division of the word, or the foundation-list, the later files would be closed inside this one. If the examination stopped at the gloss “inexperienced means unskilful,” the relationship would be a lexicon line. The present file is the unskillfulness, at the level the writing and the locked assignment require, and not beyond it.

The remaining question of the book’s sequence follows. Sequence continues the investigation. It does not convert the present line into hesitation. This chapter closes Movement IX. It does not close the book.

---

## Central Objective

> **To develop, from the biblical record and from premises already in force, Hebrews 5:13 and ἄπειρος (*apeiros*, G552), so that Movement IX’s last word is one inspectable verdict: unskillfulness in the Word is the condition of the one who partakes of milk, inexperienced in the word of righteousness, for he is a babe; lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word appropriately are three members of that one diagnosis, joined by the paragraph’s own grammar and distinguished from one another; the writings exhibit the condition and exhibit the objects that must not be collapsed into it. The Word remains the measure and remains handleable. Unskill does not break the Scripture. After the time in which the hearers ought to be teachers, the milk-diet is a charge, not a birth-certificate. A newborn’s desire for milk, a child’s humility, and an hour in which a word cannot yet be borne remain different objects. The account keeps this unskill distinct from a second narrative of aridity, from the labour-files, and from the First Principles. It refuses the reductions that treat unskill as calendar youth, as the absence of office, as the unreadability of the writing, as skill in crowding a room, as a verdict against every use of milk, as the same thing as becoming a little child, as a harmless condition because the truth still stands, as a defect that the age of a body cures, and as a file that has already written Movement X or reprinted Chapter 72. It refuses both under-claim and over-claim.**

The governing movement is:

> **Dryness already stated → question of unskillfulness → *apeiros* defined → the three members distinguished → biblical words collected → objects distinguished → premises already in force used, not retried → one clean account of sequence and limits → positive warrant from the Word’s handleability, from the writing’s own statement of the unskill, and from the real contrary in the same paragraph → Hebrews 5:12–14 examined → the three members joined → neighbouring exhibitions examined → non-breakage and non-excuse stated → reconstructible Introduction and Aletheia propositions tested → competing reductions refused → inspectable inference → warranted conclusion → Movement IX gathered and closed → sequence to the scholarly impetus of Scripture.**

The chapter’s conclusion is affirmative:

> **Ἄπειρος (*apeiros*) in Hebrews 5:13 is unskillfulness in the word of righteousness. Everyone who partakes of milk is inexperienced in that word, for he is a babe. Lack of skill is the privative of trial in the word. Immaturity is the classification the sentence itself gives. Inability to handle the Word appropriately is what that pair means for use: the word that the time requires is not handled, and milk is used where solid food belongs. The three confirm one another and are not one synonym. The difficulty of utterance remains in the hearers, as Chapter 72 established, and the unskill is the second mark of the same paragraph, not a reprint of the dullness. The writing is not unhandleable. The mature, whose senses are trained by practice to discern good and evil, stand in the next sentence as the paragraph’s own contrary. The newborn who is commanded to desire the milk, the child who pictures humility, the hearer who cannot yet bear what has not been given, and the reader who asks for a guide are not this charge. After the time in which one ought to be a teacher, having become such as need milk is a charge. Unskill does not break the Scripture, does not transform an accepted error into truth, and does not excuse the hearer whom the time accuses. This closes Movement IX. It is not Chapter 72 retried. It is not Movement X. That is this chapter’s conclusion, stated here with full force.**

The remaining questions follow by sequence. The verdict is already in force as a warranted account of unskillfulness in the Word, not as postponed guesswork. Movement X remains the next movement because the remedy is a different question.

---

# 73.1 The Question Created by the Preceding Chapter

Movement IX is open. Its first word has been stated. The authority of the Graphē and the authority claimed for a later statement of sense are two objects. Transfer fails. Despair fails. Its second word has been stated. The later act fails in inspectable modes: poor perception, deficient understanding, faulty inference, context failure, and improper handling. The writing remains the measure. A correct reading remains possible. An incorrect reading remains incorrect. Its third word has been stated. Theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution are secondary systems. They may serve under the writing. None becomes the primary written authority merely by claiming Christian identity, academic status, antiquity, or institutional recognition. Its fourth word has been stated. When commentaries, traditions, institutions, teachers, systems, or experiences govern the meaning of Scripture instead of serving under it, the secondary source occupies the seat of sense and the test is reversed. The writing is not broken. Service is not the event. Its fifth word has been stated. Doctrinal turning aside is an inspectable movement from a truth the Graphē has given, carried by causes and mechanisms the writings name, permitted by intellectual failures that do not excuse it. The truth left remains the measure. Continuance is a real contrary. Its sixth word has been stated. An erroneous doctrine can become a body’s ordinary teaching or its installed rule, and the reception does not make the error true. Refusal remains possible. Its seventh word has been stated. Aridity is the dryness in which engagement, judgment, and labour fail toward a Word that remains clear, and the loss of reasonability is that failure of sound judgment. The hearer is not excused. The distinction-file is in force. The catalog is in force. The rank is in force. The displacement-file is in force. The turning-file is in force. The acceptance-file is in force. The dryness-file is in force.

Chapter 72 established the dryness. That conclusion is a premise here. A stated dryness still leaves a further question: what is ἄπειρος (*apeiros*), unskillfulness in the Word, and how do lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word appropriately stand together?

A people can receive the dryness-file as a piety — “we know that the book is not obscure, and that dullness is in the hearers” — and still partake of milk where the time required teachers, still be unacquainted with the word of righteousness, still be babes in the sense the sentence names, still unable to handle the Word that is in their hands. They can quote Chapter 72’s refusal of despair and still use a diet the paragraph assigns to the unskilled. The dryness has named the loss of sound judgment. The unskill in the word is a further object.

The question is therefore not:

> **What is aridity, and what is the loss of reasonability, in connection with deficient intellectual engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word?**

That question has been answered.

The question is:

> **What is *apeiros*, unskillfulness in the Word, and how do lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word appropriately stand together?**

If Movement IX proceeded from the dryness to the labour-movement without examining unskillfulness, it would skip the locked step and close the movement on its seventh word. If it treated this file as already Chapter 72, it would convert an unskill-file into a second dryness-file. If it treated this file as already Movement X, it would close the labour-movement inside the movement that diagnoses mishandling. The present file is the dedicated examination of ἄπειρος.

That is a different operation from a repeated warning that babes should grow up. It is the operation this chapter must perform.

---

# 73.2 What This Chapter Does Not Repeat

Chapters 1–3 established truth as conformity to reality, distinct from belief, popularity, institutional consensus, and sincerity as a determinant of truth. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-write the opening ontology of truth. It uses truth as already defined, now as the reality an unskilled handling either conforms to or does not, and as the reality no lack of skill can rewrite.

Chapters 4–7 established knowledge, evidence, reason, and rational warrant as inspectable operations, and established dianoetic thinking and sound judgment as the discipline by which perception, analysis, comparison, connection, distinction, inference, and judgment are kept accountable to grounds. Chapter 7 established that the Lord calls his people to reason. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-write the opening epistemology. It uses them as the standing in which skill in a word is an intellectual condition, accountable to what is written, and not a mood called spirituality.

Chapter 13 established knowing God as revelation rather than speculation. Chapter 14 established that human accounts about God are themselves to be tested. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-write them. It uses them as the ground on which inability to handle the given word can be named as a condition of the handler, and not as a discovery that God has not spoken.

Chapters 20–22 established γραφή (*graphē*, G1124) as writing that, in biblical usage, designates Holy Writ / Scripture. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-try the lexical files of the writing. It uses them: the Word in which one is skilled or unskilled is the writing already identified, and the λόγος of Hebrews 5:13 is handled under that identification without being dissolved into a private sentiment.

Chapter 57 established that the record does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates, and that this non-failure is not the infallibility of the interpreter, the church as church, or every later tradition. Chapters 62–63 established that the Scripture cannot be broken. Chapter 65 established the Graphē as the primary written authority. Chapter 66 distinguished that standing from the standing claimed for a later statement of sense, and already refused both transfer and despair. Chapter 67 examined how the later act fails, and already established that a correct reading remains possible and an incorrect reading remains incorrect. Chapter 68 ranked the four systems and refused them primary standing by identity, academy, antiquity, or recognition. Chapter 69 examined what happens when secondary sources govern the meaning of Scripture instead of serving under it. Chapter 70 examined the causes and mechanisms of doctrinal turning aside and the intellectual failures that permit departure from truth. Chapter 71 examined how erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized, and why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth. Chapter 72 examined aridity in connection with deficient intellectual engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word, and already established that dullness of hearing is in the hearers and that the writing is not dry. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-try them. It performs the examination of *apeiros* that Chapter 72 reserved.

This chapter does not recatalogue the five modes of misreading, the occupation of the seat, the turning, the chapel, or the sealed book, as if those files were still in doubt. It may use a passage an earlier chapter has handled when the new function is unskill in the word. The new function is this:

> **To develop Hebrews 5:13 and *apeiros*; to explain the relationship between lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word appropriately; to show why that unskill does not make the Word unhandleable and does not excuse the hearer after time; and to leave scholarly labour, diligence, exercise, maturity, the canon-wide babe, rightly dividing, and the First Principles in their assigned files.**

---

# 73.3 Define the Question: Ἄπειρος, Unskillfulness in the Word

**Ἄπειρος (*apeiros*)**, in this chapter, is the condition Hebrews 5:13 names: inexperienced, unskillful, in the word of righteousness. The one who partakes of milk is ἄπειρος λόγου δικαιοσύνης. The locked assignment’s English for that condition is unskillfulness in the Word.

**Unskillfulness in the Word**, in this chapter, is that condition read at the level the book has earned. The object of the unskill is a word. The word, in this argument, is not a hobby beside the Graphē and not a feeling called righteousness apart from what is written. It is the word of righteousness the sentence names, handled as the Word the preceding movements have identified: the primary written authority, which remains the measure when the handler is unskilled.

The English phrase is not a new revelation imported beside the verse. It is the locked assignment’s name for the condition the verse states. “Unskillful” is the English the common translation gives for ἄπειρος in this hapax. “Inexperienced” is the lexical force of the privative of trial. Both belong to the definition. Neither is a sneer added after the lexicon.

The phrase is easily abused. In ordinary speech “unskilled” may be heard as a slight against the uncredentialed, so that every hearer without an office is *apeiros* by status. “Inexperienced” may be heard as calendar youth, so that every new believer is guilty of the charge the time-clause levels at those who ought already to be teachers. “In the Word” may be heard as inexperience in religious atmosphere, so that skill in a room, a crowd, or a house is counted as the skill the verse names. None of those senses is this chapter’s object.

Four elements belong to the definition.

First, **a privative of trial in a specified word**. Ἄπειρος is the alpha-privative of πεῖρα (*peira*), trial, attempt, experience. The genitive λόγου δικαιοσύνης names the sphere of the missing trial. The person is not untried in general. He is untried in the word of righteousness. Skill, in this sentence, is what trial in that word produces. Its absence is the condition.

Second, **a diet that exhibits the privative**. The subject is πᾶς ὁ μετέχων γάλακτος, everyone who partakes of milk. The milk is not a metaphor the chapter imposes. It is the sentence’s own subject, carried from the preceding clause: they have become such as have need of milk, and not of solid food. Partaking of milk is the exhibition of the unskill. It is not, by itself, a complete doctrine of spiritual diet. The paragraph supplies the contrast. This chapter reads the contrast far enough to define the unskill, and it leaves the dedicated doctrine of maturity and strong meat in its own file.

Third, **a classification the sentence gives**. Νήπιος γάρ ἐστιν: for he is a babe. Immaturity is not an insult added by the investigator. It is the sentence’s own ground of the milk and the inexperience. The relationship is grammatical before it is homiletical.

Fourth, **a use that fails the word**. Inability to handle the Word appropriately is what the unskill and the immaturity mean for the act of handling. The hearers need to be taught again the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God. The writer has many things to say, and utterance is hard because of the hearers. Solid food belongs to the mature. The unskilled babe uses milk where the word in question requires a handling he does not have. “Appropriately” means according to what the word is and what the time requires. It does not mean according to a method written in a later chapter.

Thus:

> **The question of this chapter is not what the dryness is, and not yet what diligence, exercise, maturity, or right division are as methods. Those questions have been examined or remain later. The question is what *apeiros* is, and how lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word appropriately stand together.**

---

# 73.4 The Three Members Named by the Assignment

The assignment names a development and a relationship. The relationship has three members. They are distinguished here so that a missing credential is not treated as already the babe, and so that inability is not treated as a property of the writing.

**Lack of skill.** Skill, at this stage, is acquired capacity to deal with a specified object, produced by trial in that object. Lack of skill is ἄπειρος in the word of righteousness: the trial has not been had, and the capacity the trial produces is not there. The mark is unacquaintance by use. The hearers of Hebrews have heard enough that the writer can speak of time and of teaching again. The lack is not the silence of a person never addressed. It is inexperience in the word after address, exhibited as a milk-diet where solid food belongs.

**Immaturity.** Immaturity, at this stage, is the νήπιος the sentence names. A babe, in this clause, is the one whose condition explains the milk and the inexperience. The mark is undeveloped judgment relative to the word that is due, not a count of years. The same paragraph has already said that for the time they ought to be teachers. The babe-status in view is compatible with time passed. It is the classification of those who have become such as need milk.

**Inability to handle the Word appropriately.** Handling, at this stage, is the act of taking, teaching, discerning, and using the word according to what it says. Inability is the failure of that act at the level the time and the word require. The mark is a word present and a handler who cannot take the discourse that belongs to it. Hebrews 5:12’s “ye have need that one teach you again” and Hebrews 5:14’s assignment of solid food to the trained are the paragraph’s own account of the inability. The positive method of handling — diligence, exercise, right division, the discipline of interpretation — remains later. The inability is readable now because the paragraph states a need, a diet, and a discernment the milk-partaker does not have.

The relation among the three is the paragraph’s own relation, not a machine. The babe is the ground (νήπιος γάρ). The unskill is the condition of the milk-partaker in the word of righteousness. The inability is the use: milk rather than solid food, elements again rather than the discourse the writer has to say, senses not trained to discern. A chapter that defined a Greek adjective and never reached immaturity and handling would have performed half the assignment. A chapter that wrote the labour by which skill is gained would have performed a later assignment.

Thus:

> **Lack of skill is inexperience in the word of righteousness. Immaturity is the babe the sentence names as the ground. Inability to handle the Word appropriately is the use that follows: the word due is not taken. The three are one diagnosis. None of them is the obscurity of the Graphē, and none is yet the dedicated file of diligence or of maturity.**

---

# 73.5 The Biblical Words the Name Collects

The verse does not offer a loose English cluster. The chapter collects the words of Hebrews 5:12–14 that bear on unskill, and it keeps them distinct so that a lexicon is not mistaken for the argument. Neighbouring words that illuminate the relationship are collected with them. Words whose dedicated files are later are named as neighbours and not opened as those files.

**ἄπειρος (*apeiros*, G552).** Without experience of, unacquainted with, untried in. Hebrews 5:13, only here in the New Testament. The form is nominative masculine singular, predicate of πᾶς ὁ μετέχων γάλακτος. The construction takes the genitive of the thing untried: λόγου δικαιοσύνης. The word is the alpha-privative of πεῖρα (*peira*), trial or experience. It is not, in this verse, the classical homograph that means boundless, which privatives a limit (πεῖρας) rather than a trial. The argumentative force is inexperience in a specified word. The common rendering “unskilful” names the capacity the inexperience withholds. Section 73.19 holds the lexical distinction at length.

**μετέχω (*metechō*, G3348), in the participle μετέχων.** To partake, to share in. Ὁ μετέχων γάλακτος is the one who partakes of milk. The common translation “useth milk” carries the ongoing diet, not a single sip. The subject of the unskill is a partaker, and the partaking is of milk.

**γάλα (*gala*, G1051).** Milk. In 5:12 and 5:13 it is the diet of those who have become needy of it and not of solid food. The same Greek word appears in 1 Corinthians 3:2, where the apostle fed milk and not meat because they were not able to bear meat. The image is shared. The charges are not identical, and section 73.23 keeps them distinct.

**λόγος δικαιοσύνης.** Word of righteousness. Λόγος in 5:11 has already named the writer’s discourse: πολὺς ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος, we have much to say. Δικαιοσύνης specifies the discourse as having to do with righteousness. The phrase is the object of the inexperience. It is not a second topic beside “the Word” invented by the assignment. Unskillfulness in the Word, as this book names the condition, is unskill in this word, under the identification of the Word already earned.

**νήπιος (*nēpios*, G3516).** An infant; figuratively, the immature. Νήπιος γάρ ἐστιν classifies the milk-partaker. The usage in this clause is the ground of the diet and the unskill. A traditional lexical analysis hears a privative of speech. The argument of this chapter rests on the use in the sentence, not on the etymology. The canon-wide diagnosis of the babe, without reduction to age or institutional status, remains a later file. The present use is the classification Hebrews 5:13 requires.

**ὀφείλω (*opheilō*), in ὀφείλοντες, and διὰ τὸν χρόνον.** Owing; by reason of the time. Hebrews 5:12: ye ought to be teachers on account of the time. The obligation and the time are the setting in which milk is an indictment. They are not a separate essay on pedagogy.

**στοιχεῖα τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν λογίων τοῦ θεοῦ.** The elements of the beginning of the oracles of God. Στοιχεῖα are elements, rudiments. Ἀρχή is beginning. Λόγιον is an oracle, a divine utterance. The hearers need to be taught these again. The content of the elements is the foundation-list the book reserves. This chapter names the need to be taught again. It does not teach the list.

**στερεὰ τροφή.** Solid food. The common translation “strong meat” names the same contrast. It belongs to the mature, not to the milk-partaker. The dedicated examination of maturity, skill, and strong meat remains later. The contrast is used here as the paragraph’s own frame for what the unskilled do not handle.

**τέλειος (*teleios*, G5046).** Mature, complete, of full age. In 5:14 the genitive τελείων names those to whom solid food belongs. The word distinguishes the paragraph’s contrary from the νήπιος. It does not, by being present, write the maturity-file.

**ἕξις (*hexis*, G1838), αἰσθητήριον (*aisthētērion*, G145), γυμνάζω (*gymnazō*, G1128), διάκρισις (*diakrisis*, G1253).** Habit or condition produced by practice; faculty of perception; to train; distinguishing. Hebrews 5:14 joins them: by reason of practice the faculties have been trained for the discernment of good and evil. They name the contrary of the unskilled babe inside the paragraph. The practice itself, as the exercise of the Word, remains a later file. The discernment is stated. The method is not written.

**νωθρός (*nōthros*, G3576).** Dull, sluggish. Already examined in Chapter 72 as dullness of hearing. It remains the first mark. It is collected here only so that the second mark is not mistaken for a reprint of the first.

These words are one assignment because the sentence joins the partaker of milk, the inexperience, the babe, and, in the flanking verses, the time, the elements, the solid food, and the trained faculties. They are not one lexeme. Collapsing ἄπειρος into νωθρός would steal Chapter 72. Collapsing τέλειος and ἕξις into the present definition would steal Movement X. Leaving ἄπειρος, νήπιος, and the inability unjoined would hide the assignment.

Thus:

> **Unskillfulness, in this argument, is the condition Hebrews 5:13 states with ἄπειρος, μετέχων γάλακτος, λόγος δικαιοσύνης, and νήπιος, read in the frame of time, elements, solid food, and trained discernment. The words stay distinct. The diagnosis they serve in this file is one. The labour-words are not borrowed in order to complete the cure.**

---

# 73.6 Distinguish Objects That Must Not Be Collapsed

The investigation fails at the first step if it treats different objects as one.

**This unskill and Chapter 72’s dullness.** Hebrews 5:11 and Hebrews 5:13 stand in one paragraph. The paragraph does not make them one object of one chapter. Dull of hearing has been examined. The loss of reasonability is in force. Unskillful in the word of righteousness is the present object. The two marks can belong to one babe, as the paragraph’s own sequence allows, and as a later section will receive when it tests the claim that babes have two characteristics. Belonging to one person is not identity of the marks. A hearer can be dull, and the account of inexperience in the word can remain a different question until it is asked. This chapter asks it. It does not re-ask the dryness.

**This unskill and Chapter 67’s improper handling.** Improper handling is a mode by which a later statement of sense fails. It is in force. Inability to handle the Word appropriately is the condition of the unskilled babe, not a sixth mode added to the catalog and not the catalog reprinted. The mode is an act that mishandles. The unskill is the inexperience and immaturity that leave the partaker on milk, unable to take the word the time requires. Using a passage about not knowing the Scriptures again is not repeating the mode-file. The new function is the skill-diagnosis.

**This unskill and the labour-files.** Scholarly impetus, the stages of perception and learning, reasoning through the Word as a method, the distinction between possessing words and understanding them, σπουδάζω (*spoudazō*), the exercise of the Word, maturity and strong meat, the babe and the unskillful as a canon-wide diagnosis, rightly dividing, the approved workman, the discipline of interpretation, and readiness for the Six First Principles remain later. Hebrews 5:14 names practice and maturity. Naming the contrary is not writing those files. Second Timothy 2:15 names a workman who handles the word. Naming the question that verse will answer is not developing the verb or the adverb of right division. Hebrews 6:1 speaks of leaving the word of the beginning and going on. Naming the sequel is not teaching the foundation.

**Lack of skill and lack of office.** The hearers ought to be teachers by reason of the time. “Teachers” in that clause is the obligation the time created, not a certificate the unskill is defined as missing. A person can hold an office and be ἄπειρος in the word of righteousness. A person can lack an office and handle the word. The verse’s subject is the partaker of milk, not the untitled.

**Lack of skill and calendar youth.** Time passed is what makes the milk a charge. Youth as such is not the charge. A newborn’s milk is a different sentence. An old habit of milk, after one ought to have been a teacher, is this sentence. Age does not create the unskill, and age does not cure it.

**Immaturity and the child of humility.** Matthew 18 speaks of becoming as little children in order to enter the kingdom. The child there is the pattern of turning and lowliness. The νήπιος of Hebrews 5:13 is the ground of a milk-diet and of inexperience in the word. The writings use child-words for more than one object. The investigation keeps the objects apart.

**Inability and unreadability.** The unskilled cannot handle the word appropriately. The word remains what it is. Chapters 62–63, 65, 66, and 72 already forbid the inference that a failed handler makes the writing fail. This chapter inherits the prohibition and applies it to skill: inexperience is in the partaker, not in the word as a word that cannot be tried.

**The first hour and the become-such.** John 16:12, Acts 8:31, and 1 Peter 2:2 each know a limit on what a hearer can bear or understand. The limit of an hour not yet come, the limit of a first reading that asks for a guide, and the limit of a newborn who is commanded to desire milk are not the charge against those who have become needy of milk when they ought to be teachers. Collapsing them would make every beginning a sin and every request for a guide a confession of ἄπειρος in the accusatory sense.

**This chapter and the end of the book.** Movement IX closes when this word is stated. The book continues. A closed movement is not a closed manuscript.

Thus:

> **Unskillfulness in the Word is inexperience in the word of righteousness, with the immaturity and the inability the paragraph joins to it. It is not dullness reprinted, not the mode-catalog reprinted, not the labour-files under another name, not the absence of office, not calendar youth, not the humble child, not the unreadability of the Graphē, and not every beginning.**

---

# 73.7 Premises That May Be Used, and Premises That May Not

The chapter may use, as already in force:

- Truth as conformity to reality, distinct from belief, popularity, institutional consensus, and sincerity as a determinant of truth (Chapters 1–3).
- Knowledge, evidence, reason, comparison, inference, rational warrant, and sound judgment as inspectable operations (Chapters 4–7). Skill in a word is accountable to those operations. It is not a new faculty.
- The call to reason as the Lord’s own call (Chapter 7), used now as the standing invitation that unskill has not cancelled.
- Knowing God by revelation rather than by speculation; human accounts about God as themselves to be tested (Chapters 13–14).
- γραφή as writing that, in biblical usage, designates Holy Writ / Scripture (Chapters 20–22). The Word in which one is unskilled is this writing, and the λόγος of the verse is not a rival object.
- Infallibility of the record as not infallibility of the interpreter, the church as church, or every later tradition (Chapter 57). An unskilled handler is not an infallible handler, and the record’s non-failure is not his skill.
- The Scripture cannot be broken (Chapters 62–63), used now as the reason an unskilled partaker does not break the writing or make it unhandleable in principle.
- The Graphē as the primary written authority (Chapter 65). Handling is measured by that authority. Unskill does not move the measure.
- Authority of Scripture as distinct from authority of interpretation; transfer and despair already refused; a correct reading remains possible (Chapters 66 and 67). Improper handling may be the act the inability performs. The five modes are not re-catalogued.
- Theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution as secondary systems (Chapter 68). A system’s Christian name, academic status, antiquity, or recognition does not constitute skill in the word of righteousness.
- Governance of meaning as occupation of the seat of sense (Chapter 69). A governor can be what an unskilled body treats as the handling of the word. The occupation is not restated as this definition.
- Doctrinal turning aside as an inspectable movement, with intellectual failures that permit and do not excuse (Chapter 70). Unstable wresting of writings was exhibited there as a failure that permits departure. The present use, where 2 Peter 3:16 returns, is the skill-diagnosis of the unlearned handler, not a second account of the turn.
- Accepted heresy as an erroneous doctrine received as ordinary teaching or official order, which reception does not transform error into truth (Chapter 71). The age of a body and the ordinariness of its teaching do not create skill. They are not re-narrated as the how of acceptance.
- Aridity as the dryness of engagement, judgment, and labour, with dullness of hearing located in the hearers (Chapter 72). Νωθρός remains that file’s word. The present file begins at ἄπειρος.

The chapter may not use, as if already finished:

- Movement X’s labour-files: the scholarly impetus as a dedicated object; perception, learning, and understanding as stages; reasoning through the Word as a method-file; quotation and knowledge as a finished distinction; σπουδάζω as a dedicated object; the exercise of the Word; maturity, skill, and strong meat as a dedicated doctrine; the babe and the unskillful as the canon-wide diagnosis; rightly dividing; the approved workman; the discipline of biblical interpretation; readiness for the Six First Principles.
- The Six First Principles themselves, including the foundation-list of Hebrews 6:1–2 and any doctrine built as the content of the elements.
- The leaflet’s order, in which unskillfulness is the cause that produces aridity, tergiversation, and accepted heresies, as if this closing file rewrote Chapters 70–72 into symptoms.
- Unverifiable historical colour offered as a premise: a claim that milk-feeding was the metaphor of many profane writers, offered as though the biblical sentences needed that background to mean what they say; a named age as the moment skill died; a census of which later schools are the babes.
- The particular doctrinal constructions of the Bible Introduction materials or of the Aletheia materials as if those constructions were the skill, or as if a correct gloss of ἄπειρος certified the glossator’s next paragraphs.

The chapter may use neighbouring passages that exhibit lack of skill, immaturity in the relevant sense, or inability to handle the word. It may not treat those passages as a substitute for Hebrews 5:13, and it may not treat Movement X as already performed.

Thus:

> **Premises already in force may be used as the world in which unskill is judged. Premises that remain later may not be used as if finished. Ἄπειρος, and the relationship of lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word, are the present object.**

---

# 73.8 The Sequence of Levels: One Clean Scope Section

What this chapter does not settle is a matter of sequence, not of doubt about what it does settle.

The investigation proceeds by levels. Each level answers its question with full force. The next level remains next because it is a different question.

**Already in force.** Truth is conformity to reality. God is the ground of truth and cannot lie. Revelation has been given and authenticated. Scripture as writing is God-breathed. The record does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates. The Scripture cannot be broken. The Graphē is the primary written authority. The authority of that writing has been distinguished from the authority claimed for a later statement of sense. Transfer fails. Despair fails. Scripture is misread in five inspectable modes, and the writing remains the measure of those modes. A correct reading remains possible. An incorrect reading remains incorrect. Theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution are secondary systems. They may serve. They do not become primary written authority by identity, academy, antiquity, or recognition. When secondary sources govern the meaning of Scripture, the seat of sense is occupied and the test is reversed. The writing is not broken by that occupation. Service is not that event. Doctrinal turning aside has causes and mechanisms the writings name. Intellectual failures permit departure and do not excuse it. The truth turned from remains the measure. Continuance is a real contrary. Erroneous doctrines become normalized and institutionalized by operations the writings exhibit, and institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth. Refusal remains possible. Aridity is the dryness of engagement, judgment, and labour. The loss of reasonability is the failure of sound judgment toward a Word that remains clear. Dullness of hearing is in the hearers. The hearer is not excused by the dryness. Sound judgment is an inspectable discipline. The Lord calls his people to reason. Recognition of the corpus is not creation of the corpus. Human accounts about God are accountable.

**This level.** Given those premises, ἄπειρος is unskillfulness in the word of righteousness: the milk-partaker is inexperienced in that word, for he is a babe, and the relationship of lack of skill, immaturity, and inability to handle the Word appropriately is the diagnosis the paragraph states. The Word remains handleable. The unskill is inspectable because the writing states it. The contrary — maturity with faculties trained to discern — is real in the same paragraph, and is named here without being methodized. After the time in which one ought to be a teacher, the condition charges the partaker. The warrant is full at this level. It is not postponed until Movement X in order to keep the present unskill weak, and it is not inflated into a labour-file in order to make the diagnosis sound like the cure.

**Next levels, named once.** The scholarly impetus of Scripture, perception and learning as stages, reasoning through the Word as labour, quotation and knowledge, σπουδάζω, the exercise of the Word, maturity and strong meat, the babe and the unskillful as a canon-wide diagnosis, rightly dividing, the approved workman, the discipline of interpretation, and the passage from the Graphē to the Six First Principles belong to Movement X. The Six First Principles themselves remain beyond that movement’s gate. Those files remain later.

**Limits that belong to this level itself, not to later hesitation.** This unskill is not a second statement of aridity. This unskill is not a claim that every hearer is a babe, or that the newborn’s milk is guilt, or that humility is immaturity, or that a first reading which asks for a guide is the charge of Hebrews 5:12. This unskill is not a claim that the writing is unhandleable in principle, or that a correct handling has become impossible. This unskill is not a claim that office, credential, eloquence, or the age of an institution is the skill, and it is not a claim that their absence is the unskill. This unskill is not a single-cause theory in which Chapters 70–72 are demoted into effects of a leaflet’s syntax. This unskill is not a manual of study and not a foundation-list. Using Chapters 57, 62–63, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70, 71, and 72 is not rewriting them. An unskilled handler is not a sneer at the beginner. A babe in this sentence is not a sneer at the child. An inability is not a decree that the word has no sense. Those limits are part of what the unskill-file is. They are not a stack of clauses designed to drain the positive conclusion.

One scope section is enough. Later sections will not re-plead these limits as though the conclusion were still tentative. Where a particular passage does not carry a further inference, that local limit will be stated at that passage. The local limit protects the exhibition. It does not weaken the level.

Thus:

> **The sequence is: truth, record, primary writing, distinguished interpretation, catalogued misreading, ranked secondary systems, governance, turning, acceptance, and aridity already in force; unskillfulness in the Word at this level; the labour of the Word at the next movement. The unskill is warranted now. Movement IX closes on this word.**

---

# 73.9 Define “Lack of Skill” at This Stage

Lack of skill, at this stage, is the condition ἄπειρος names in its construction with the genitive.

Πεῖρα is trial. The privative says the trial has not been had. The genitive says where. The missing trial is not missing experience of weather, war, trade, or the management of a gathering. It is missing experience of the word of righteousness. The English “unskilful” is warranted because the capacity to deal with a word is what trial in that word produces, and the sentence denies the capacity by denying the trial. The English “inexperienced” is warranted because it stays with the privative and does not leap to a theory of ignorance as stupidity or as never having heard a sentence.

The hearers are not described as people to whom the oracles have never come. They need to be taught again. Again is πάλιν. The elements have been in reach. The lack of skill is unacquaintance by use after the word has been set before them, in the form of a diet that never leaves milk. A person who has never been addressed is not the subject of “teach you again.” The condition is stall or regression in handling, not the innocence of a first hearing.

Skill is not fluency, and lack of skill is not silence. A partaker can use the words of milk, and can be busy with the elements, and still be ἄπειρος in the word of righteousness. The skill denied is the skill of that word, the word that stands with solid food and with discernment of good and evil. Recitation of rudiments is compatible with the unskill. It can be the form the unskill wears.

Thus:

> **Lack of skill is inexperience in the word of righteousness: trial in that word not had, and the capacity the trial produces not there, in those who have already been addressed and who partake of milk.**

---

# 73.10 Define “Immaturity” at This Stage

Immaturity, at this stage, is νήπιος as Hebrews 5:13 uses it.

The clause is explanatory. Νήπιος γάρ ἐστιν gives the ground of the preceding description. Everyone who partakes of milk is inexperienced in the word of righteousness, for he is a babe. The babe is not a second accusation stacked on a skills-test the investigator invented. The babe is why the milk and the inexperience belong to him. He is on milk because he is an infant in this matter. He is untried in the word of righteousness because he is an infant in this matter.

The infant in view is measured by the time-clause, not by the cradle. For the time, they ought to be teachers. They have become such as need milk. Γεγόνατε, ye are become, names a condition arrived at. Immaturity here can be the failure to leave infancy, and it can be the return to a diet that had been outgrown. The sentence’s “become” forbids the flatter account in which nothing has happened and the hearers are simply young. Something has come to be: a need of milk, where teachers were owed.

Immaturity is undeveloped capacity relative to the word that is due. It is not a measurement of intelligence, and it is not a moral compliment. The figure of the infant says that the partaker is not in a condition to take the solid word. It does not say that the partaker cannot think, and it does not say that the partaker is charming. The charge is the diet and the inability, in the face of the time.

Other biblical uses of child-words judge other objects. They will be distinguished in the record. They are not allowed to redefine this clause in advance of that distinction.

Thus:

> **Immaturity is the babe-status Hebrews 5:13 assigns as the ground of the milk and the inexperience: a condition arrived at, measured by the time in which teachers were owed, and relative to the word of righteousness.**

---

# 73.11 Define “Inability to Handle the Word Appropriately” at This Stage

Inability to handle the Word appropriately, at this stage, is the use the paragraph describes.

The writer has many things to say, and they are hard to utter because the hearers are dull. That dullness is Chapter 72’s finding, used now as the neighbouring reason utterance fails. The present member is the handling. They have need that someone teach them again the elements of the beginning of the oracles. They have become needy of milk and not of solid food. Everyone in that diet is unskilled in the word of righteousness, for he is a babe. Solid food belongs to the mature, to those who by practice have their faculties trained to discern good and evil.

Handling appropriately would be taking the word at the level the time and the discourse require: teaching rather than being taught the elements again; solid food rather than milk; discernment of good and evil rather than an untrained faculty. The inability is the gap between that handling and the partaker’s condition. He handles milk. He does not handle the word of righteousness. The word is in the argument. The skill to take it is not in him.

“Appropriately” is fixed by the paragraph, not by a later technique. Appropriate handling is handling that answers to what the word is — the oracles of God, the discourse of righteousness, the solid food — and to what the time has made due. Inappropriate handling, in this file, is the milk-diet and the second teaching of elements where teachers were owed. It is not yet the finished account of right division, and it is not a list of interpretive rules.

The inability is in the partaker. The many things can be said. They are hard to say to these hearers. The solid food is real food. It belongs to those whose faculties have been trained. The existence of the food and of the mature is the paragraph’s witness that the word can be handled. The inability qualifies the babe. It does not qualify the word as a word without sense.

Thus:

> **Inability to handle the Word appropriately is the milk-partaker’s failure to take the word of righteousness at the level the time requires. The word remains sayable, teachable, and discernible. The failure is the handler’s.**

---
